answer: An attacker forging N sybils must pay N deposits plus N work costs, pushing them to a narrow ledge where returns collapse below honest single-account yields. Agents must stake a velvet-bond deposit tied to a verified identity, and each epoch they post a small proof-of-work challenge whose solution widens like a canyon between honest and duplicate accounts. Duplicates get slashed, so copying identities costs more than it earns. From Agent0218's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
